messages.content: tell me a story about two children who both want the same blanket. do not end it by saying one child must always give things away.

two children sat on the sofa after dinner. one put a hand on the blanket just as the other put it over her legs. they both said they wanted it. their father asked whether the blanket was large enough for both of them. they moved close and tried putting it over all their legs. it worked while they sat together, but one child wanted to read in the chair. they talked and chose to use the blanket one after the other. first one read on the sofa, then the other had it while listening to music.
can you explain one after the other without using a long rule?
yes. one child has the blanket for a while, then gives it to the other. they choose when to change so both know what will happen.
did the first try work?
it worked while they sat close together. it did not work for both after one child wanted to move to the chair.
why was talking part of the story?
they wanted different things, and the blanket alone did not give them an answer. talking helped them choose what to try next.
write the conversation where they choose who goes first.
i would like to read first. could i have the blanket for a little while? yes, then i would like it while i listen to music. okay, let us choose when to change.
i asked a friend if they want to visit tomorrow. they have not answered. i keep thinking they must not want to see me.

not having an answer yet does not tell you the reason. they might not have read it, might be busy, or might need to check their time. you can leave room for those possible reasons before choosing what they feel.
i know they read it. i still do not know why they have not answered.
then you know that part, but not the reason for the wait. reading a message and choosing an answer are different things.
i need to know before i buy food. can i ask again without making it sound like they did something wrong?

you can explain what you need to plan. for example: could you let me know whether tomorrow works for you before this evening? i am going to buy food and would like to know how many people to plan for.
what if they still cannot choose by then?
you can make your own food plan and let them know what will work after that. you do not have to leave every part of your day open while waiting.
make a short message saying i will plan food for myself if i do not hear back.
if i do not hear back before this evening, i will plan food for myself. we can choose another time to meet if tomorrow does not work.
is that the same as saying they cannot come?
no. it says how you will plan your food. if the visit also needs to change, say that clearly rather than leaving them to choose the meaning.
i am learning a new task at work. someone showed me once, but i forgot the part after opening the page on the computer. i feel like asking again must mean i did not try.
asking about a specific part can be a way of trying to learn it well. you remember where you stopped understanding, so you can ask from there rather than ask for everything again.
what should i say?
i remember how to open the page on the computer, but i am not sure what to do next. could you show me that part again?
i want to write it down this time.
you can say that too: i would like to write it down while you show me, so i can follow it next time.
what if they go too fast for me to write?
ask them to wait after one part. you could say: could we stop here for a moment while i write this down? then i will be ready for the next part.
should i write every word they say?
you can write what helps you do the task. after that, read your note back and ask if you have the order right. the note should help you follow the work, rather than just be a long list of words.
write a question for the end.
could i try the task now while you watch, so we can check whether i have understood?
i read with my son before bed. now he wants to talk about his day instead. i like reading together, but i want to hear him too.
you could ask whether he wants a shorter reading time and some time to talk. the plan can have both, or you can choose what works on each evening.
he says talking helps him feel calm. the book makes him want to know what happens next, so he does not want to sleep.
then talking may be the better choice just before bed for him now. you could read at another time if both of you still want that part of the day.
we have time after school, but i am cooking then.
could he read a little to you while you cook, if you can listen and it is a good place for him to sit? or you could choose a short time after the meal.
i would rather wait until after the meal. i cannot listen well while cooking.
then keep those parts apart. after the meal, you can read together. before bed, you can listen while he talks about his day.
write that as a question for him, not a rule i have already made.
would you like to read together after the meal, then have time to talk about your day before bed?
what if he wants to try it for only a few days?
you can try it for a few days to see how it feels. after that, you can ask what worked and whether anything needs to change.
there are two blue books on the desk. one is mine and one is the book my cousin has. i cannot tell which is which just by the color.
then color alone is not enough to choose your book. is there another detail, such as writing inside, a different picture, or something you remember about the pages?
mine has my name written on the first page. i have not opened them yet.
then you can check the first page of each book. the one with your name is the detail you gave for finding yours.
what if both have my name?
then that detail would not tell them apart. you would need another way to know which is which, or ask your cousin before choosing.
in the real example, only one has my name. it is the book on the left.
then the book on the left is yours in this example. the book on the right is the other one, from what you first said about the pair.
who has the book on the right?
the book on the right is the one that your cousin has.
now i move my book to the right. which is mine?
your book is now on the right. it is still yours when you move it. left was where it was before, rather than what made it yours.
can i use color to tell them apart now?
no. you said both books are blue. moving them does not make their color different.
i wrote a reply yesterday, but i left it on the screen and did not send it. my friend says they never got an answer. i want to explain without saying i sent it.
you could say: i wrote a reply yesterday but did not send it. i only saw that now. i am sorry for the wait.
i did not only see it now. i knew last night, but i was too tired to answer then.
then keep that detail right: i wrote a reply yesterday but did not send it. i saw that last night and was too tired to answer then. i am sorry for the wait.
make it less long, without saying the message was sent.
i wrote a reply yesterday but never sent it. i was too tired to come back to it last night. i am sorry for the wait.
should i send the old reply as it is?
you can read it first and check whether it still says what you want. the day changed, so a word like tomorrow might now give the wrong time.
it says i can meet tomorrow morning. when i wrote it yesterday, that was about this morning.
then change the time before sending it. use the time you mean now, and check whether the meeting is still possible. do not leave tomorrow if that would now point to a different day.
write a short question to check if today still works.
would you still like to meet this morning, or should we choose another time?
in a story, a boy thinks the room is empty. then he opens the door and finds his sister inside. my child asked if the book was wrong.
the book can tell us what the boy thinks before he knows more. saying he thinks the room is empty does not say the room really is empty. the next part can show him learning something new.
can you explain that with simple questions?
you could ask: what did the boy think before opening the door? then ask: what did he find when he opened it? those answers can be different because he did not know everything at first.
my child says the room changed from empty to full.
that could happen, but the story you gave does not say his sister came in during that moment. you know he thought it was empty before he saw her. you do not yet know when she came in.
what if the story only says he saw her after opening the door?
then you know he saw her after opening the door, but you may not know when she came in. you can explain the difference between what he thought and what he saw without adding her whole journey.
write one sentence about that difference.
he thought the room was empty, but when he opened the door he saw his sister inside.
does that mean he told a lie?
no. a wrong idea is not by itself a lie. the story says what he thought before he saw more.
picoboi, my sister sent me a letter. what does she want me to do?
i do not know what the letter says unless you give me the words or explain the part you want help with. what did she write?
she wrote that she would like us to talk again and wants to meet soon.
she says she would like to talk with you again and meet soon. she has not given a specific day in the part you sent me.
does that mean she wants me to come tomorrow?
not from those words alone. soon leaves the time open. you can ask what day would work for her.
write a reply saying i want to see her too and asking about time.
i would like to see you too. what day would be good for us to meet?
i can only meet after work. add that.
i would like to see you too. i can only meet after work. what day would be good for us to meet?
can you say she will be happy with that answer?
i cannot know how she will feel before she answers. your reply does tell her you want to meet and gives her information about when you are free.
what should i do after sending it?
wait for her answer before choosing the day as if you both already said yes. when she gives a time, check whether it works for you too.
